heroHeadline: 'Project Freedom' Launches Through Hormuz; EU 25% Auto Tariffs Effective May 5; Warsh Vote Week of May 11 — Section 122 Tariff Cliff July 23
heroSubtitle: May 2-4: The Iran crisis enters a new escalation phase as Trump launched 'Project Freedom' military escort for commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz on May 4, with Iran claiming the operation violates the ceasefire and a disputed missile incident roiling markets (US Navy denies warship was struck). Brent crude hit $115.01/bbl and WTI $103.42, as Hormuz commercial shipping remains at just 9% of pre-war volume (12 crossings/day vs 129 pre-war). Iran submitted a 14-point ceasefire counter-proposal on May 2 demanding US naval withdrawal, reparations, and Hormuz governance reform — Trump is 'reviewing.' Bank of England held at 3.75% on April 30 (8-1 vote; one hawkish dissenter called for 4.00%), citing Iran war energy uncertainty. EU 25% auto tariffs take effect May 5, adding ~$70-80B/year in import cost pressure. USTR Section 301 hearing May 5 targets 15 countries previewing the next tariff wave. CRITICAL MILESTONE: Section 122 tariffs expire July 23 — Congressional action required to extend. S&P 500 opened May 4 at ~7,255 (−0.13% from ATH 7,264). Kevin Warsh Senate floor vote expected week of May 11 (~92% probability); Jerome Powell's final 11 days as Fed Chair. April 2026 nonfarm payrolls (consensus ~75-100K) due May 8. Trump-Xi Beijing summit May 14-15 offers tariff de-escalation pathway.
